kinds.description: The single source-of-truth map of src/'s module boundaries and responsibilities. A stale citation here usually means that module's real responsibility shifted — re-read the section and confirm it still describes what the file actually does, don't just re-stamp the hash.

The package's own index, linking every sibling doc. A stale citation to a sibling usually means that doc was restructured — confirm the link still points at the right section, not just that the file still exists.

States why this work matters, grounded in a cited spike (see this package's grounded_by rule). If that spike changed, re-check whether it still supports the stated need — a changed spike can quietly invalidate the whole problem statement.

Ranks directions against a cited spike's evidence. If that spike changed, re-check whether the ranking or a rejected option's reasoning still holds — a stale citation here can mean a decision now rests on outdated evidence.

Real, run feasibility evidence, not narrated. If the code this spike cites changed, the primitive it once confirmed working may no longer be — don't assume it still is; re-run the spike or downgrade the citing doc's confidence.
Maps the real user workflow to a walking-skeleton release scope. If a cited doc changed, check whether the walking skeleton it marks out is still accurately described.
Sequences shippable releases, grounded in a cited spike and derived from a cited story-map. A stale citation to either means the sequencing rationale may need re-justifying, not just re-stamping.

Concrete enough to implement from directly, built on a cited spike's validated primitive (see this package's builds_on rule). If that spike changed, confirm the primitive is still validated before trusting this doc's approach.

Reusable lessons, sourced from a cited spike. If that spike changed, re-verify the lesson still accurately reflects it — a lesson can quietly go stale even when the underlying technique is still fine.

rules.description: Requires design-package's _SUMMARY.md to link its own problem-space.md. A stub or copy-pasted problem-space.md (no real need/context, root cause, or honest evidence basis) satisfies this link while adding nothing — read it, don't just trust the link.
rules.name: requires

rules.description: Requires design-package's _SUMMARY.md to link its own solution-space.md. A solution-space.md listing one option with no real alternative considered, or no rejects recorded, satisfies this link while being hollow — read it, don't just trust the link.
rules.name: requires

rules.description: Requires design-package's _SUMMARY.md to link its own spikes.md. A spikes.md that narrates what an experiment 'would probably show' instead of a real run satisfies this link while proving nothing — this check cannot tell the difference.
rules.name: requires

rules.description: Requires design-package's _SUMMARY.md to link its own story-map.md. A story-map describing internal engineering tasks relabeled as 'stories' (not a real user workflow) satisfies this link while missing the point — this repo's own story-maps have this exact gap.
rules.name: requires

rules.description: Requires design-package's _SUMMARY.md to link its own roadmap.md. A roadmap with no dependency reasoning behind its sequencing, or that ignores its own cited spike/story-map (see grounded_by, derived_from), satisfies this link while being arbitrary.
rules.name: requires

rules.description: Requires design-package's _SUMMARY.md to link its own implementation-details.md. A doc that restates the roadmap at a higher abstraction, rather than being concrete enough to start from, satisfies this link while not doing its job.
rules.name: requires

rules.description: Requires design-package's _SUMMARY.md to link its own knowledge.md. A knowledge.md that recaps what the rest of the package already said, instead of a lesson someone extending this later actually needs, satisfies this link while adding nothing new.
rules.name: requires

rules.description: A cost/feasibility/risk claim in solution-space.md must cite the spike backing it — direction runs FROM the claim TO its evidence. Citing a spike that tested a different primitive, or one cited elsewhere in the package but unrelated to THIS claim, satisfies the link while proving nothing.
rules.name: grounded_by

rules.description: A sequencing decision in roadmap.md must cite the spike justifying it — direction runs FROM the ordering TO its evidence. A spike cited in passing, with no bearing on why this increment comes before or after another, satisfies the link while explaining nothing.
rules.name: grounded_by

rules.description: A risk/investment claim in problem-space.md must cite the spike backing it — direction runs FROM the claim TO its evidence. A spike that merely exists in the same package, without actually demonstrating the claimed risk, satisfies the link while proving nothing.
rules.name: grounded_by

rules.description: implementation-details.md's approach must cite the spike that validated its primitive — direction runs FROM the approach TO the confirming evidence. A spike that tested a different primitive, or an inconclusive/failed run, satisfies the link while the approach stays unvalidated.
rules.name: builds_on

rules.description: knowledge.md's restated lesson must cite the spike it came from — direction runs FROM the lesson TO the spike, so a reader can check it's still accurate. If the spike changed since, the lesson can be quietly wrong while the link stays satisfied.
rules.name: sourced_from

rules.description: A roadmap concept (e.g. a walking skeleton) must cite the story-map it realizes — direction runs FROM the roadmap increment TO the story-map that defined it. A coincidentally-linked story-map, not the one the increment actually realizes, satisfies the link while misrepresenting it.
rules.name: derived_from

rules.description: problem-space.md must link the originating GitHub issue — the evidence basis the whole package rests on. Linking any issue matching the URL pattern, rather than the actual source of the stated need, satisfies this link while making the 'evidence basis' fictitious.
rules.name: traces_to
